# Client

`JaegerClient` is the entry point. Create one per process (or per set of credentials), share
it between threads/tasks and close it on shutdown. Service functions hang off the client (see
[Functions](functions.md)).

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep functions — service-owned: client functions and their Jaeger behaviour; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

| Function | Returns | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| constructor / `create` / `new` | client | validates the config (`CONFIG` error) |
| `fromEnv()` | client | config from `GROW_JAEGER_*` and the vendor variables (`JAEGER_QUERY_URL`, `JAEGER_SAMPLING_ENDPOINT`) |
| `health()` | `HealthStatus { healthy, status, details }` | `GET /` on the query port without the token, plus healthcheckv2 detail when `healthUrl` is set; **never throws** for an unhealthy or unreachable service, only for `CANCELLED` and `CONFIG` |
| `ping()` | latency | authenticated round trip (`GET /api/v3/services`); `AUTHENTICATION` when an auth proxy rejects the token |
| `serverVersion()` | version string (`2.23.0`) | from the UI page, else `target_info` at `metricsUrl`; `UNSUPPORTED` when neither reports one |
| `buildInfo()` | `gitVersion`, `gitCommit`, `buildDate` or null | from the UI page |
| `samplingStrategy(service)` | sampling strategy | one fetch from `samplingUrl` |
| `query` | `JaegerQueryClient` | trace queries ([Trace queries](functions/query.md)) |
| `initTracing(config)` / `remoteSampler(service, pollInterval)` | tracing handle / sampler | use the client's settings; closed by `close()` |
| `close()` | — | idempotent; flushes tracing handles, stops samplers created through the client |

`status` is `ok`, `degraded` (healthcheckv2 reports a problem), `unhealthy`, `unreachable` (network
error) or the vendor's word. Every function with an example per language: [Client functions](functions/client.md).

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

## Create, use and close

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep examples — service-owned: create/use/close examples per language; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { JaegerClient, JaegerConfig } from "@grow-codes/jaeger";

    const client = new JaegerClient(new JaegerConfig({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:16686" }));
    const health = await client.health();          // { healthy, status, details }
    const latencyMs = await client.ping();         // number (ms)
    const version = await client.serverVersion();  // string
    await client.close();                          // safe to call twice

    // Cancellation and per-call deadline: every I/O method accepts { signal }
    const status = await client.health({ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2_000) });
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use grow_jaeger::{JaegerClient, JaegerConfig};

    let config = JaegerConfig::builder().url("http://127.0.0.1:16686").build()?;
    let client = JaegerClient::new(config)?;
    let health = client.health().await?;          // HealthStatus
    let latency = client.ping().await?;           // Duration
    let version = client.server_version().await?; // String
    client.close().await;                         // safe to call twice

    // Cancellation: drop the future, e.g. with a deadline
    let status = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2), client.health()).await;
    ```

    Without an async runtime, enable the `blocking` feature:

    ```rust
    let client = grow_jaeger::blocking::JaegerClient::from_env()?;
    let health = client.health()?;
    ```

=== "Go"

    ```go
    client, err := jaeger.NewClient(jaeger.Config{
        CommonConfig: jaeger.CommonConfig{URL: "http://127.0.0.1:16686"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer client.Close() // safe to call twice

    health, err := client.Health(ctx)         // HealthStatus
    latency, err := client.Ping(ctx)          // time.Duration
    version, err := client.ServerVersion(ctx) // string

    // Cancellation and deadlines come from ctx
    ctx2, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    health, err = client.Health(ctx2)
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from grow_jaeger import CancelToken, JaegerClient, JaegerConfig

    with JaegerClient(JaegerConfig(url="http://127.0.0.1:16686")) as client:
        health = client.health()           # HealthStatus
        latency_ms = client.ping()         # float (ms)
        version = client.server_version()  # str

        # Cancel from another thread
        token = CancelToken()
        health = client.health(cancel=token)
    # close() ran; calling it again is safe
    ```

    `AsyncJaegerClient` has the same methods as coroutines (`await client.health()`,
    `await client.aclose()`, `async with`), and honours task cancellation.

=== "Java"

    ```java
    JaegerConfig config = JaegerConfig.builder().url("http://127.0.0.1:16686").build();
    try (JaegerClient client = JaegerClient.create(config)) {
      HealthStatus health = client.health();
      Duration latency = client.ping();
      String version = client.serverVersion();

      // Async variants return CompletableFuture; cancel(true) cancels the request
      CompletableFuture<HealthStatus> pending = client.healthAsync();
      pending.orTimeout(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS).join();
    } // close() is idempotent
    ```

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

## Lifecycle rules

- The client is safe for concurrent use. Reuse it: it keeps a connection pool.
- `close()` flushes queued work (for example log batches) within the configured deadline and is
  safe to call more than once. Any call on a closed client fails with `CANCELLED`
  (`"<operation>: client is closed"`).
- Each language also offers its idiomatic scope: TypeScript `try/finally`, Rust `close().await`
  (plus best-effort `Drop`), Go `defer client.Close()`, Python `with`/`async with`, Java
  try-with-resources.
